visual_appeal: Reduce the visual competition between segmented XP bars, portrait rims, row dividers and chip borders. Keep the four state colours, but render bar segment dividers at roughly 20% opacity and row dividers at #493B28.

Establish three text tiers consistently: primary information #F0E5CA, secondary information #C8BDA9, tertiary metadata #A79C89. Preserve class-coloured names and state-coloured labels; stop giving almost every supporting line the same cream emphasis.
state_colours: In the exhausted-rest toast, the green left rail currently accompanies a warning about the current character. Use the current character's relevant warning colour on the rail, and reserve green for the recommended character's Full label and portrait accent.

Add a small numeric percentage beside each timeline character name. The orange lanes currently look equally full despite representing substantially different rested amounts; state colour alone cannot explain them.
Keep the chip family, but give its text 4 px horizontal inset and use consistently sized 12 px state icons. The current narrow chips crowd the icons and lettering.
character_identity: Recompose the saved-look character card: place a 128–144 px portrait at the upper left and the speech bubble to its right with a 16 px gap. The current upper-right portrait leaves a large dead area and disconnects the speech from its speaker.

Move the level badge into the character metadata line rather than leaving a tiny black circle attached to the portrait. Retain the class badge on the saved face and the race/gender badge on class-icon fallbacks.
Replace Acct #3 and the options choice #3 with a player-defined account alias, falling back to Account 3. Keep the alias in a secondary 12 px treatment rather than competing with the character name.
default_theme: Darken the roster surfaces slightly toward #211B14 and reduce the amber saturation of their outlines. The default scene still reads as stacked brown boxes rather than a single composed panel.

Apply a #100D0A overlay at approximately 35% opacity to the hero background artwork, strongest behind its text. Preserve the oak-and-bronze chrome, but make the illustration subordinate to the recommendation.
Standardize default-theme buttons to a 24 px height, 12 px horizontal text padding and a quieter #705735 border; the gold action strip and gold buttons currently compete for attention.
elvui_wc3_fit: Without altering Gatewood's supplied art or frame seams, standardize addon-owned interior panel padding to 12 px and use the same near-black content fill across roster, character card and alerts.

Use the configured ElvUI body font for addon-owned metadata, options and alert text, while retaining the display treatment for titles. Match the real Character window's stronger distinction between bright labels and secondary information.

Reduce addon-owned gold rules to #79623C and reserve brighter gold for active tabs and important headings. This will sit more quietly beside the supplied Character and Options windows without requiring WC3-specific skin code.
alerts_ux: The logout banner tells the player to cancel but only offers Details. Add a 24 px-high Cancel logout button if the client API permits it, followed by a secondary Details action; otherwise explicitly say Cancel the logout countdown, then hearth to an inn.

Make the exhausted-rest toast lead with Le Jette: no rested XP in at least 13 px text, then Play Le Dette on the next line. The current first line is too subordinate for the event that triggered the notification.
In move mode, show a dashed outline labelled Esc menu anchor above its attached card. This makes attachment understandable even when the actual menu is hidden; keep the existing Reset behaviour.
Give every alert dismissal control a minimum 24 × 24 px hit target, even if its visible close artwork remains smaller.
readability: Increase roster supporting text and ETA text to at least 13 px at native UI scale, with 15 px names and 12 px minimum helper text. This is a size and hierarchy issue, not a criticism of the simulator's narrower font rendering.

The primary roster still omits calendar timestamps for most characters. Use a stable two-line ETA block: 21% · Full in 7d 21h, then Wed 2 Dec, 01:36 in secondary text. Increase row height from roughly 58 px to 66 px if necessary.
Rewrite Full since 1d 16h ago: rest is going to waste. as Full for 1d 16h · further rest is wasted. The current grammar is awkward and the sentence is longer than its information warrants.

Raise timeline date-gutter text to 12–13 px and add 8 px clearance after the arrow tips. The current small dates are among the most useful information in that view but receive one of its weakest treatments.
layout_polish: Rebuild roster rows on fixed columns: 24 px rank, 48 px portrait, flexible identity, 244 px progress/ETA and 116 px state, with 12 px gutters. Align all chip edges and all bar starts to these columns.

Move the character card's XP bar and full-time text into its main content panel, immediately below the name and metadata with a 12 px gap. The edge-to-edge bar floating between two bordered panels looks assembled rather than designed.

Give the timeline a visibly labelled After 48h gutter with a subtle vertical separator. All long-duration lanes currently terminate at the same place, making the graphic look more informative than it actually is.

In options, place the Move notifications helper below its button instead of extending across the page. Use 16 px between sections and 24 px setting-row spacing; keep the existing two-column alert group.

Reserve a consistent 40 px footer across roster and timeline, with 12 px side insets and vertically centred controls. The current footer feels packed against the lower frame compared with the spacious hero.
delight: Make character speech more specific to saved context: a location-aware line such as Thunder Bluff has excellent napping spots is more characterful than Comfy here. Keep lines short enough for two lines at 14 px.
Add a restrained 400 ms gold-to-state accent transition when the recommended character changes, respecting Reduce motion. Avoid adding another shimmer to an already ornamented interface.
Add a short contextual timeline summary above the lanes, such as Next full: Le Bankken in 19h 11m. This turns the view into a useful anticipation moment rather than just a set of long coloured lines.

overall_notes: A substantial improvement over the real baseline: the recommendation is unmistakable, the empty current-character bar is gone, and the shared alert treatment is more coherent. I would not yet approve this as a 9-level demanding-user release. The remaining problems are information hierarchy, incomplete calendar-time presentation in the main roster, an under-composed saved-look card and a timeline whose identical long lanes communicate little about actual rested amounts. The default theme is credible but still over-outlined; ElvUI mode is recognizably compatible without being fully typographically integrated. I have not deducted for simulator model limitations, prescribed portrait fallbacks, class-coloured names, the four state colours or Gatewood-owned frame artwork.
